newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar storm kills 15 after cyclone disaster.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar storm kills 15 after cyclone disaster.

text.p: A storm killed at least 15 people in northwestern Madagascar two weeks after a cyclone left an estimated 200 people dead or missing, state radio said on Tuesday.
It said tropical depression Josie in the last few days killed 15 people including four hit by falling debris after heavy rain storms led to severe flooding in some areas of the northwest.
The worst-hit town in the vanilla-producing region was Maroantsetra, where the mayor told the radio residents took to small boats because its streets were completely flooded.
The radio added that other towns, such as Vohemar and Antalaha, were virtully cut off because roads were damaged.
Josie struck the northwest as rescue work continued in the southeast after Cyclone Gretelle, which the Red Cross estimates left 200 people missing or dead and affected some 520,000.

France agreed to send a second Transall transport plane and a second Puma helicopter from its island base at Reunion to help in the southeast at the request of newly elected Madagascar President Didier Ratsiraka.
In his inaugural address, Ratsiraka who was sworn in on Sunday said his government would built 35,000 homes each year in the southeast and he had received some aid from donors for the programme.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said last Friday Cyclone Gretelle destroyed up to 90 percent of villages in the southeast when it hit between January 24 and 26.
